name: decrement_strong_count_in
declaration: unsafe fn decrement_strong_count_in (ptr : * const T , alloc : A)
rules: For Arc::decrement_strong_count_in(ptr, alloc), ptr must have been obtained through Arc::into_raw.
If ptr was obtained from Arc<U, A>::into_raw and U is sized, U must have the same size and alignment as T.
If ptr was obtained from Arc<U, A>::into_raw and U is unsized, U's data pointer must have the same size and alignment as T.
If ptr reinterprets an original type different from T despite matching size and alignment, the reinterpretation must satisfy the validity requirements of both the original type and T.
When Arc::decrement_strong_count_in(ptr, alloc) is invoked, the associated Arc instance must be valid: its strong count must be at least 1.
For Arc::decrement_strong_count_in(ptr, alloc), ptr must point to a block of memory allocated by alloc.
The caller of Arc::decrement_strong_count_in must ensure that a specific value of T is dropped only once.
Arc::decrement_strong_count_in may be used to release the final Arc and its backing storage.
Arc::decrement_strong_count_in must not be called after the final Arc has been released.
